meta.title: Restarting the example queue worker takes four steps and can be undone in two
meta.lede: Use this when the example queue stops draining and the worker needs a clean restart. Background in [r1].
meta.foot: Source: an invented example. Replace every command and value with your own.

purpose: Bring the queue worker back to a healthy state without losing queued jobs.

preconditions.item: You can reach the example cluster from your terminal
preconditions.check: The cluster status command prints a version.

preconditions.item: No deploy is running right now
preconditions.check: The deploy dashboard shows no active run.

preconditions.item: The on-call engineer knows you are about to restart
preconditions.check: You posted in the on-call channel.

steps.title: Confirm the queue is stuck
steps.expect: The depth is above 500 and has not fallen in five minutes.

steps.title: Pause new intake
steps.expect: The output says the queue is paused.

steps.title: Restart the worker
steps.expect: The output says one worker restarted and is ready.

steps.title: Resume intake and watch it drain
steps.expect: The depth falls for three checks in a row, one minute apart.

rollback.title: Pause intake again
rollback.expect: The output says the queue is paused.

rollback.title: Return to the previous worker release
rollback.expect: The output names the earlier release and says it is ready.

escalation.when: The depth keeps rising ten minutes after the restart
Jobs are lost or run twice
